title: ACL Surgery: Choosing a Graft - Hamstring, Patellar Tendon or Quadriceps?
metaDescription: Choosing a graft for ACL reconstruction: hamstring, patellar tendon, quadriceps or donor graft compared simply, with pros and cons.
intro: No single graft suits everyone in ACL reconstruction. A 2025 review says the choice should suit your age, sport, other health issues and recovery goals. Each graft trades something: strength, pain at the donor site, or speed of healing. Your surgeon should explain why they recommend one for you.

sections.heading: What are the options?
sections.body: The new ligament is built from a tendon. It can be taken from your own hamstring, your own patellar tendon (below the kneecap, with small bone blocks), or your own quadriceps tendon. A donor tendon (allograft) can also be used.

sections.heading: What is used most often?
sections.body: The hamstring. In a large Swedish registry of nearly 40,000 ACL operations, hamstring was used in about 94 out of 100, patellar tendon in 4 and quadriceps tendon in 2. Practice differs between countries.

sections.heading: Hamstring or patellar tendon?
sections.body: Hamstring is very strong and usually causes less pain at the front of the knee. Patellar tendon heals faster because bone joins to bone, but pain at the front of the knee is more common. Neither is proven better for everyone.

sections.heading: What about the quadriceps tendon?
sections.body: A growing option. Reviews suggest less donor-site pain than patellar tendon with similar function, but long-term evidence is less than for the other two grafts, and it depends on the surgeon's experience.

sections.heading: When is a donor graft used?
sections.body: Mostly for revisions or when several ligaments are injured, because it avoids harvesting your own tendon and shortens surgery. Some studies report higher failure with certain donor grafts.

sections.heading: How should I decide?
sections.body: Ask which grafts your surgeon uses regularly, why they recommend one for you, and what recovery to expect. Recovery and return to sport depend on rehabilitation as much as the graft.

faqs.q: Which ACL graft should I choose?
faqs.a: It depends on you. No single graft suits everyone.

faqs.q: Which ACL graft has the lowest re-tear rate?
faqs.a: Studies are mixed, so no graft can be called safest for everyone.

faqs.q: Does a hamstring graft weaken my leg?
faqs.a: Some hamstring weakness can occur; rehabilitation helps.
